newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts see Kimber Q3 sales up.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see Kimber Q3 sales up.

text.p: Two analysts said on Monday that they expected sales to improve in third-quarter earnings reports for paper company Kimberly Clark de Mexico due to the economy picking up and the consolidation of Compania Industrial de San Cristobal (Crisoba).

"We estimate sales of almost 2.2 billion pesos in 3Q96, mainly due to the consolidation of Crisoba results, up by 12 percent year-over-year," Jesus Viveros, an analyst with the Valores Finamex brokerage, said in a report.

Julio Zetina, analyst at the GBM brokerage, told Reuters: "We foresee healthy growth in sales volumes of around 28 percent compared to the third quarter last year, basically due to incorporating San Cristobal. The third quarter also sees a seasonal upswing due to the beginning of the school year."
The pulp and paper sector had been hit very hard the economic crisis that followed the sudden devaluation of the peso in December 1994.
But both analysts said the sector was showing signs of recovery and should post improved results in the third and fourth quarters of this year.
Zetina added that world prices for pulp, one of the paper industry's main inputs, fell during the quarter ending September 30 and this would help Kimber's operating margins.
"Margins will be better and operating earnings should increase to 29 percent of sales, compared with 26 percent a year ago," Zetina said.
